pricingBasis: Cloudflare Workers Paid Standard account minimum plus included usage and listed overage rates; D1 and R2 independently metered
sensitivityOnly: Per-login and per-registration provider CPU are unmeasured. 10ms and 100ms are illustrative; 600ms is a conservative sensitivity near but not equal to local bcryptjs Workerd elapsed samples, and is NOT billed CPU evidence.

routeSourceMap.login: POST /auth/login -> AuthService.validateCredentials (existing-account bcrypt compare; unknown email exits early)
routeSourceMap.publicImageGet: GET /public/listings/:id/images/:imageId -> ListingsService.getPublicImage (image/listing lookup + R2 GetObject Class B)
routeSourceMap.adminImageGet: GET /admin/listings/:id/images/:imageId -> AuthGuard user revalidation + ListingsService.getAdminImage (image/listing/owner-role lookup + R2 GetObject Class B)
routeSourceMap.imageDelete: DELETE /listings/:id/images/:imageId -> AuthGuard user revalidation + ListingsService.removeImage (owner listing + image lookup, R2 GetObject before free DeleteObject, D1 delete + dense-position compaction)
routeSourceMap.imageReorder: PATCH /listings/:id/images/:imageId -> AuthGuard user revalidation + ListingsService.reorderImage (owner listing, ordered D1 load, bulk position reset, per-image position updates, ordered result read)

assumptions.imageGetTrafficSplit: Assumed 95% public / 5% ADMIN image GETs in every scenario; counts sum to total modeled API-mediated image GETs.
assumptions.loginCpuModel: Each modeled login is conservatively assumed to reach the bcrypt compare path (existing account with wrong password or equivalent costly verification); unknown-account paths observed in source skip bcrypt and would cost less.
assumptions.registrationCpuModel: Each registration is assumed to execute one bcryptjs cost-12 password hash. The same 10/100/600 assumed provider CPU ms sensitivities are applied; local elapsed hash time is not billed CPU evidence. Source performs no explicit user lookup; D1 read factor is zero, while engine-level unique-index work is unmeasured.
assumptions.attackSensitivity: Monthly request-volume sensitivity only. Burst concurrency, provider throttling, source IP reputation, anti-abuse controls, and account-wide shared traffic are not quantified.
assumptions.ownerAdminRouteDriverScope: Other OWNER/ADMIN calls including edit/upload subdrivers; excludes ADMIN image GET and image DELETE/PATCH reorder, which have separate explicit route drivers.

cpuSensitivity.label: elapsed-proxy sensitivity only; not metered CPU

optionalDurableObjects.unresolvedBecause: No DO actor/lock topology or monthly request count, active GB-s, SQLite rows-read/written, or storage volume is established. If introduced, these charges are additive to Workers and D1/R2 scenario use; no DO cost is assumed to be zero.
billingNotes: Inactive objects do not incur duration until active; idle objects not eligible for hibernation remain billable.
Billable excess for each dimension rounds up to the provider billing unit.
Deletes count as SQLite rows written; key-value-style operations use hidden SQLite rows.

caveats: Not a quote, forecast, or authorization to buy/enable billing; traffic and data counts are hypothetical.

Workers Static Assets are excluded from Worker request count; all modeled dynamic route drivers include POST /auth/register, login, and API-mediated image GET, image DELETE and image PATCH reorder operations.
D1 rows-read factors are route-level scan assumptions; only local/production meta.rows_read and query plans can validate them.

D1 write factors are simplified planning proxies: edits = listing+audit+one average index row; image upload = metadata+two average index rows; contact = one row; registration = one user row plus primary-key and unique-email index rows; deletion = one deleted image row plus shifted rows and one average index-mutation factor; reorder = two position updates per image with table plus index row mutations. Actual D1 metadata counters may differ.
High case deliberately models a large unindexed catalog scan (15,000 rows/query) and abuse-sensitive login volume to expose cost and availability risk.
R2 operation billing rounds total operations up to whole million-operation units before included units are subtracted; storage is rounded to whole GB-month in this model.

R2 object deletion itself is treated as free on Standard, but each modeled image delete includes one source-parity read-before-delete GetObject Class B operation; failure compensation re-Put, retries, object listing, metadata HEAD, multipart and account-shared usage are omitted.
No account hard spend ceiling or automatic hard cap is assumed. Workers per-invocation CPU limits are not monthly bill caps.

Durable Objects are excluded from scenario totals and explicitly unresolved: their request, active duration, SQLite row-read/write and storage meters are listed separately; no DO workload or necessity/proof exists in this task.
